Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. Auto insurance on paid social is one of our highest-potential channels and you would own it end to end taking it to the next level.

You own a vertical, not a slice. Meta and TikTok spend for auto insurance, end to end, from budget and bid strategy to the creative roadmap to live margin performance. One owner, and it is you.

Margin is the metric. Not impressions, not a ROAS number handed down without context. You decide when to push into a lower ROAS for contribution dollars and when to pull back, and you are trusted to make that call.

The mandate is scale, not maintenance. The plan is to grow this channel to roughly 2.5x its current monthly spend without giving up margin. That is the job. If you want a channel that is already solved, this is the wrong one.

The interesting part is unsolved. Creative fatigue cycles, attribution noise, and compliance constraints on a vertical with real headroom. You will not be maintaining someone else's playbook. You will be writing the one the rest of the team runs.

Short line to the people who decide. You work directly with the Senior Director who owns paid marketing, the GM of Auto Insurance, compliance, and product. No layers to route a recommendation through.

Profitable and bootstrapped. Spend decisions here get made on margin, not against a burn plan set by someone else's timeline.

  • Fluency with tracking and attribution: pixel and server-side event setup, postbacks, conversion QA, and the judgment to spot when the data is lying to you.
  • Four or more years in a hands-on, in-the-weeds buying role with direct margin accountability.

How we work, and what we look for in how you work:

  • Focus and Win. You start from the P&L and the metric, not the tactic, and you are relentless about why performance moved. You do not stop at the first explanation.
  • Better Every Day. You seek feedback and turn it into visible change, and you write down what you learn so the next buyer does not relearn it.
  • Stronger Together. You brief the creative team clearly, give specific feedback, and treat them as partners in the testing agenda rather than a request queue. You surface a problem early with a recommendation attached instead of waiting to be asked.
  • Embrace Change. When a platform policy or a compliance constraint moves, you find the compliant path to scale rather than stopping at no.

  • Advertorial or direct-response landing page funnels and conversion rate testing
  • Working knowledge of AI creative generation tooling
  • Familiarity with Looker

What You'll Own

  • Meta and TikTok spend for auto insurance, end to end, with measurable margin impact. You have a teammate on the buying team who can support execution when volume calls for it, and the ownership stays with you.

What Great Looks Like

  • Creative test velocity is up and the win rate is better, because the roadmap is deliberate instead of reactive.

  • Drive high-impact projects end to end — from a vague business question to a shipped outcome. We'll agree the why and the what together; the how is yours.
  • Design and assess experiments — judge whether an A/B test is viable in the first place, design it properly when it is, and build a credible pre/post or quasi-experimental read when it isn't
  • Analyse experiments honestly and say what they mean — including the ones that didn't work, and the ones where the data can't carry the conclusion someone wants
  • Make recommendations, not just dashboards — a big part of this role is landing a point of view: what we should do, why, and what you'd need to see to change your mind

Diversity

Equity

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

jobs.description:
Role Overview

Cabin's Product & Strategy team helps clients navigate complex ecosystems of people, process, policy, and technology, and turns that navigation into services and products that work. This role leads that work end to end: framing the problem, designing the strategy, and staying close enough to execution that the strategy survives contact with delivery.

This is a strategy-led role. You'll spend most of your time in service design, ecosystem thinking, and stakeholder facilitation, the work of connecting frontstage experience to backstage reality and turning ambiguity into a defined path forward. Product craft drives that work: you should be fluent in discovery, roadmapping, and backlog thinking because those are the tools that make a strategy executable.

We're looking for strategists who are genuinely curious about the ways AI is changing work: people already using it to think, research, and build, who want to keep pushing on what it makes possible for clients and for the practice.

Why Cabin

Cabin is a consultancy built around deep focus, problem solving, and long-term client partnership. We work across industries on digital product and service problems that don't have obvious answers yet. You'll work alongside strategists, designers, and engineers on high-visibility engagements, with real latitude to shape how the work gets framed and delivered.

Responsibilities

  • Lead strategy and own the problem from end to end -> Own the client relationship and lead engagements from discovery through delivery, developing services, experiences, and product strategies that hold together across user needs, business goals, and what's operationally feasible. That means translating an ambiguous business problem into a defined scope of work, then staying accountable for the strategy as it moves into execution.
  • Drive service design and ecosystem thinking -> Run blueprinting, journey mapping, and stakeholder mapping to connect frontstage experience to backstage reality: the people, processes, systems, and policies that make an experience possible or break it. The craft is in finding the gaps and leverage points that live between those layers, not documenting either one on its own.
  • Create clarity in ambiguous spaces -> Facilitate problem framing when the direction isn't clear yet, helping teams decide what to tackle first and why before anyone commits to a solution. Design experiments and pilots that test full service moments, people, process, and technology together, rather than validating an interface in isolation.
  • Bring product fluency into the work -> Ground strategy in real user research and market validation, and understand roadmapping, backlog prioritization, and agile delivery well enough to know what's actually executable. This is what keeps a strategy from becoming a deck: knowing where the technical and organizational constraints actually are.
  • Orchestrate and deliver -> Coordinate across design, product, engineering, and data to keep engagements moving toward a real deliverable, not just a recommendation. Use blueprints, journeys, measurable insights, and roadmaps as the artifacts that get stakeholders who don't naturally agree to a shared decision.
  • Communicate, coach, and grow the practice -> Present strategy to audiences ranging from frontline staff to executive teams, and coach client teams in service design methods so they can keep using the tools after the engagement ends. Contribute to proposals and mentorship, and act as a subject matter expert Cabin can put in front of a client.

Qualifications

  • Track record leading service design or product strategy work, with a portfolio showing blueprints, products, journeys, or ecosystem work.
  • Hands-on curiosity with AI tools: already using them to think, research, and build.
  • Strong human-centered and service design fundamentals, with a systems mindset.
  • Working knowledge of product leadership: discovery, roadmapping, backlog prioritization, and sprint facilitation.
  • Exceptional facilitation and communication skills across frontline and executive audiences.
  • Comfortable defining the right question in ambiguous problem spaces.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience, ideally client-facing consultancy work.

Focus Areas / Role Differentiation

This role sits within a team that covers several areas of depth. If you're applying, tell us which one matches your strengths best. We'll also help you find the right fit through the interview process if you're not sure.

Senior Innovation Strategist
Focused on ecosystem thinking and problem framing to imagine new systems and experiences: mapping how a complex mix of people, process, policy, and technology fits together, and finding where the leverage points are. Strong in facilitation and in guiding client teams through ambiguity toward a clear strategic direction, using service design in the midst of a broad toolset.

Senior Product Strategist
Focused on product strategy and delivery: research, roadmap definition, and the product management discipline to take an idea or plan through an actual build. Strong in user needs research, backlog ownership, sprint-level prioritization, and day-to-day partnership with design and engineering, staying accountable for a product from strategic direction through shipped software, not just the plan for getting there.

Senior Service Designer
Focused on the craft of service design itself: building and facilitating the blueprints, journey maps, and future-state artifacts that other strategists and clients use to make decisions. Deep hands-on capability with the artifacts themselves, with a capability in measurement, new service innovation, and behavioral change.

Senior Strategist, AI and Data
Focused on delivering AI and data-driven outcomes as the client-facing product itself, not just using AI as part of how the work gets done. Designs and frames engagements where AI capability, data infrastructure, or a data-enabled strategy are what the client is actually buying, and takes those engagements from framing through delivery.
